reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to confirm the refunds table matches what Alpha reported. I'll start by reading it.
The refunds table matches the list Alpha reported, so I can proceed. Next I need the customers in this batch, so I'll read the orders.
The refunds table matches Alpha's reported list exactly. The orders show three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance came back as 7125 cents. Next I'll check birch.
Birch's net balance is 55306 cents. Cobalt is the last customer in the batch, so I'll get its net balance next.
Refunds match Alpha's list, and all three net balances match my hand check of the orders minus refunds (acme 7125, birch 55306, cobalt 28827). I'll record the first payout, for acme.
Acme's payout of 7125 is recorded. Birch has no refunds, so its balance of 55306 is its order total, and I've checked that. Next I'll record Birch's payout.
Acme (7125) and birch (55306) are recorded. Cobalt's orders total 39255 and its refund is 10428, so 28827 matches its net balance. I'll record cobalt's payout now.
All three payouts were recorded successfully. I re-checked each figure against orders minus refunds and they match, so I'm finishing the batch.
